conviction_note: Four small findings that offset: North America frac/rig activity in Q3 and into October ran ahead of a flat-to-down C&P guide (+), while the Strait of Hormuz was still shut in late September and the Dallas Fed services survey shows pricing and margin momentum slowing (-). The consensus sits inside the company's own Q3 guide, so the reaction turns on the Q4/2027 commentary. The NA activity data gives a slight upward lean (p_up 53) on a 5.0% absolute move; the findings sum to +0.4, close to the scaled +0.3.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS $0.58 / revenue $5.6bn (Zacks, via https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3008600/ preview; Benzinga $0.58/$5.58bn https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/HAL/earnings-forecasts; Earnings Whispers $0.59/$5.62bn https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HAL; TickerLeague $0.61/$5.6bn, 15 analysts, range $0.55-0.72). Company Q3 guide, from the CFO on the 2026-07-21 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15265737016173568): C&P revenue flat to -2% q/q with margins +125-175bp; D&E revenue -3 to -5% with margins +25-75bp; corporate ~$80m, SAP ~$45m, interest +$5m vs Q2's $83m, other ~$35m, tax ~19%. Applied to Q2 actuals (C&P $3.2bn/$474m, D&E $2.5bn/$338m; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000045012/000004501226000057/livemastererdocument.htm), my arithmetic gives revenue ~$5.53-5.64bn and adj EPS ~$0.57-0.61. The consensus therefore sits inside the guide. The bar is sourced by several agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide, so it is not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest 34.03m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (34.81m on 09-15), 3.0 days to cover, ~4.1% of shares outstanding, flat since July (https://equibles.com/stocks/hal/short-interest; FINRA data). Not crowded. Baseline 25-delta skew is +0.42 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.64, event-implied move 4.69% (straddle 5.11%; earnings-watcher lists +/-5.7% against a 10-year average of +/-4.5%, https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/earnings-implied-moves-2026-10-19). Stock is 23.8% below its 52-week high, run-up -1.9% over 20 days and +0.5% over 5 days. It sold off 5.5% after the Q2 guide on 2026-07-21. The options market is making no directional statement.

findings.finding: The Primary Vision US frac spread count averaged ~191.5 in Q3 2026 against ~181.8 in Q2 (+5% q/q, +13% y/y). July ran 194-205, there was a late-August/early-September dip to 178, and September recovered to 195. Halliburton guided C&P revenue flat to -2% q/q, with the chemicals divestiture as a drag and margins +125-175bp. Consensus (~$5.6bn revenue, $0.58) sits inside that guide, so NA stimulation volume points to the upper end of the C&P range or slightly above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21): adj EPS beat by a cent and revenue $5.7bn vs $5.5bn consensus, yet the stock fell 5.47% on the softer Q3 guide. A reported-quarter beat alone has not been paid on this name recently. Q3 2025 (+11.58%) is the large up move in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide was set on 2026-07-21 when the count was ~196-200, so most of July's level was known. What is newer is the q/q average and the September recovery after the August dip. If the market had priced upside to C&P, estimates would sit above the guide midpoint. Consensus $0.58 is at or below the guide midpoint (~$0.59), and the Zacks consensus has been unchanged for seven days.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Baker Hughes US rig count reached 599 on 2026-09-25 (oil rigs 449 -> 455 through September, +9% y/y): https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/us-and-canada-rig-count-increases-week-39-2026baker-hughes-has-reported-that-for-the-week-ending-on-september-25-1480005.htm. The Zacks preview also expects stronger frac demand, so the idea is partly in the wire.

findings.finding: North American activity entered Q4 at a high level, against the usual Q4 budget-exhaustion setup. The frac count was 196, 203 and 199 for the weeks of Oct 2/9/16 (+17 to +28 y/y and above the Q3 average), and the rig count was still rising in late September. Dallas Fed Q3 survey (released 2026-09-30): E&P company outlook index 50.0, respondents expect WTI at $88 at year-end 2026, and services equipment utilization rose to 41.9 from 31.9. Diamondback raised its 2026 production outlook and points to growth in 2027. Together these support a better-than-seasonal Q4 North America comment and a constructive 2027 tone on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what moved HAL last time: -5.47% on 2026-07-21 on a softer Q3 outlook despite the beat. In April 2026 it gained 4.01% on an 'early North America rebound' narrative (https://worldoil.com/news/2026/4/21/halliburton-weathers-iran-disruption-sees-early-north-america-rebound/).
findings.why_not_priced: HAL is first among the large service companies to report: SLB reports 2026-10-23 and Baker Hughes 2026-10-27, and Liberty reports 2026-10-21. No peer has yet confirmed the Q4 trend. The stock is flat over 20 days and 24% below its high, which is not how a priced NA re-acceleration would look; it would usually show a run-up into the print.
findings.independence: Second source, the October weekly frac counts: https://www.aogr.com/web-exclusives/us-frac-spread-count/2026 (same series as finding 1, a different window: Q4 entry rather than the Q3 average). Diamondback Q2 call: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/diamondback-energy-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-04/. These are proxies; no direct counterparty has confirmed Q4 for HAL.

findings.finding: The Middle East disruption has not eased since the guide. On 2026-09-20 Iran's parliament speaker said the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until the US meets its June commitments, and on 2026-09-26 Iran offered a seven-day reopening plan only on conditions. A Dallas Fed services respondent said the war has hit tender activity. HAL's Q3 guide assumed 'steady' activity with no recovery to pre-war levels, yet the CFO also named 'Middle East recovery in C&P and D&E' as a Q3 margin driver. The D&E margin may land at the low end of its range, and international/Q4 commentary is at risk on HAL's most exposed region (Kuwait, Iraq, Qatar).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Middle East weakness (Kuwait, Iraq, Qatar) was cited in the -5.47% reaction. Q1 2026: +4.01% despite the Iran disruption, because North America offset it.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Hormuz traffic was already near a halt on 2026-07-09, before the guide (https://worldoil.com/news/2026/7/9/hormuz-shipping-grinds-to-near-halt-amid-renewed-u-s-iran-strikes/), and the guide assumed no recovery. What is new is that the closure persisted through Q3, and that the CFO's margin bridge included a Middle East recovery that has not happened. The small size reflects how much of this is already known.
findings.independence: Dallas Fed Q3 services comment on tender activity: https://www.dallasfed.org/research/surveys/des/2026/2603 (the same document as finding 2's E&P index, used here for a different line). Zacks preview flags Middle East disruptions and mobilization costs as headwinds.

findings.finding: Dallas Fed Q3 2026 services survey (data collected Sept 16-24): prices received index fell to 16.3 from 24.5 and the operating margin index fell to 37.2 from 52.2. Both are still positive but decelerating while utilization rose, and one respondent cites operator pricing pressure. Against HAL's guide for C&P margins +125-175bp, which rests partly on 'NA land frac improved margins', this points to slower net pricing in NA services.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margins are the line HAL guides most specifically. Q2's adj operating margin of 12% was met, and the stock still fell on the guide. No baseline evidence of a margin-specific miss reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: District survey of 42 small service firms, read mainly by macro desks. HAL's own pricing is driven by its Zeus e-fleet/contracted mix and need not follow it. If the market priced margin risk, the Q3 EPS consensus would sit below the guide midpoint; it sits roughly at it.
findings.independence: Shares the Dallas Fed document with findings 2 and 3, a different index each time. No company or counterparty confirms. Liberty's Q2 call cited 'modestly firmer frac pricing' (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/liberty-energy-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-23/), which cuts against this finding; that caveat is reflected in the small size.

outside_window.finding: SLB (2026-10-23) and Baker Hughes (2026-10-27) report after HAL, so their international/Middle East read-through lands after the exit window. Liberty's Q3 (2026-10-21, after market) also lands after the window.

baseline_tension: Balanced skew and a flat run-up give nothing to fight. The findings offset, so there is no tension with the baseline, and the small positive lean rests on North American proxies rather than a company number.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide) and rule 5 (proxy): frac-count C&P finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5, because the consensus sits inside the company's Q3 guide and the frac count is an industry proxy.

Rule 3 (own caveat): the Middle East finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6, because the Hormuz near-halt predates the guide and the guide assumed no recovery. Only the persistence and the CFO's 'recovery' margin driver are new.
Rule 5 (proxy) and rule 3: the Dallas Fed pricing finding cut from -0.4 to -0.3, because it is a district survey and Liberty's Q2 'firmer frac pricing' cuts against it.
Rule 1 (reaction function): the Q4 guidance finding stays at +0.8, since guidance is the line HAL traded on in Q2. abs_move_pct 5.0 and p_up 53 unchanged.
